World English Bible British Edition, eBible.org, https://ebible.org/engwebpb/

The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this
translation):
> "The World English Bible British Edition is a Public Domain translation of the Holy Bible into contemporary British/International English. This edition only contains the 66 books of the Old and New Testament.."
> "The World English Bible British Edition
The World English Bible British Edition is not copyrighted. It is in the Public Domain. However "World English Bible" is a Trademark."
> "You may copy, publish, proclaim, distribute, redistribute, sell, give away, quote, memorize, read publicly, broadcast, transmit, share, back up, post on the Internet, print, reproduce, preach, teach from, and use the World English Bible as much as you want, and others may also do so. All we ask is that if you CHANGE the actual text of the World English Bible in any way, you not call the result the World English Bible any more. This is to avoid confusion, not to limit your freedom. The Holy Bible is God's Word. It belongs to God. He gave it to us freely, and we who have worked on this translation freely give it to you by dedicating it to the Public Domain."

Why this is public domain:
A British-English edition of the World English Bible. eBible.org states that it is not copyrighted and the translation team dedicates it to the public domain, as quoted below; a dedication of this kind applies everywhere, in the United States and in the country of origin.

The verse-per-line archive holds the Bible text in one file, one verse per line, each line starting with its reference (book, chapter:verse); its SQL and XML copies of the same text, eBible.org's description page, style sheet and signature are left out of the source.

Sources of these facts: eBible.org's details page
(https://ebible.org/details.php?id=engwebpb) and the edition's own files.
